explanation: `Prod.GameAdd.recursion` is defined (line 111–115) literally as `@WellFounded.fix (α × β) (fun x => C x.1 x.2) (hα.prod_gameAdd hβ) (fun ⟨x₁,x₂⟩ IH' => IH x₁ x₂ fun a' b' => IH' ⟨a', b'⟩) ⟨a,b⟩`. The theorem is the fixpoint equation of that `fix`, i.e. `WellFounded.fix_eq` (Init/WF.lean:139: `fix hwf F x = F x (fun y _ => fix hwf F y)`) with the motive `C ∘ Prod.fst/fst`... precisely `fun x => C x.1 x.2`, the relation `hα.prod_gameAdd hβ`, `F := fun ⟨x₁,x₂⟩ IH' => IH x₁ x₂ fun a' b' => IH' ⟨a',b'⟩` and `x := (a,b)`, after unfolding the definition of `GameAdd.recursion`; hence it is a one-line instance of that single core declaration. (The other `GameAdd.recursion_eq` at line 204 concerns `Sym2.GameAdd` and is a different statement; no separate Mathlib theorem states this equation for `Prod.GameAdd.recursion`.) Note also that the mathematical content here is purely the definitional unfolding of the library's own `GameAdd.recursion` via the general well-founded recursion principle, so one could equally regard it as not carrying independent content.
